key_insight: The paper mines OpenAI’s 2026 AI-generated mathematics release to identify reusable “mathematical instruments” — new lemmas, constructions, inequalities, and proof mechanisms — across 38 problem families.
engineering_relevance: It provides a structured way to extract, compare, and track candidate proof components that could inform future automated theorem proving and formal verification workflows.
method: Surveyed 38 families from 722 AI-written manuscripts across two groups of 17 and 21
Recorded each family’s claim, extracted instruments, antecedents, and caveats
Added cross-cutting patterns and a scoreboard for formalization status and dependencies
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a corpus-level review spanning 372 problem families, with selected source comparisons and a formalization/dependency scoreboard, but no Lean development was compiled or kernel-checked.
watch_item: Novelty and correctness assessments are explicitly provisional, and the survey does not independently certify the underlying proofs.
paper_title: What the Machine Invented: Mining New Mathematical Instruments from OpenAI's October 2026 Release of AI-Generated Mathematics
